hero.title: Run any CLI agent in a real terminal. Review its changes without losing sight of the code.
hero.desc:
The agent stays in the terminal.
The code stays in view.
Pine brings them together.
mini.nativeDesc: Built like a real Mac app, not a browser pretending to be one.
mini.focusedDesc: Agents stay in the terminal while Pine shows who is working, what changed, and when attention is needed.
mini.leanDesc: Lightweight user grammars, tasks, and keybindings — no extension marketplace or browser runtime.
mini.practicalDesc: Status in the tree, branch switching, and diff markers directly in the editor.
release.title: One continuous loop. From agent command to code review.
release.desc: Pine keeps the terminal, task context, and edited files in one native workspace, so you always know what the agent is doing and where to review it.
release.li1: Run any CLI agent in a real terminal
release.li2: See every task and return to its exact session
release.li3: Review code, Git changes, and diagnostics beside the agent
release.li4: You review and decide; Pine does not replace the tools in the loop
why.title: Keep the whole task together.
why.desc: Open related projects in one window, switch without duplicates, and keep each editor and terminal exactly where the work belongs.
why.keepsLi1: Add, switch, and close projects without multiplying windows
why.keepsLi2: Tell same-named projects apart with concise path context
why.keepsLi3: Route Agent Inbox tasks back to the window that owns them
why.keepsLi4: Suspend background editor services until a project returns
why.cutsLi1: Agents remain ordinary CLI processes in real PTYs
why.cutsLi2: Files remain files; Git remains Git
why.cutsLi3: LSP servers and formatters stay replaceable
why.cutsLi4: No proprietary prompt or transcript lock-in
why.feelsDesc: Pine lets projects, terminals, and agent tasks share one native workspace while keeping the current decision in focus.
features.title: Everything needed to edit beside an agent.
features.desc: Pine stays a focused code editor while making terminal-driven, agent-assisted work visible.
features.01title: See agent work as it happens.
features.01desc: Tracks durable tasks across projects in Agent Inbox, routes to the exact live session, and sends private notifications for verified events or detected process exits.
features.02title: Edit with native speed and real code intelligence.
features.02desc: Bundled language grammars, LSP diagnostics, completion, hover, go-to-definition, code actions, rename, symbols, folding, minimap, and project search.
features.03title: Shape one workspace around multiple projects.
features.03desc: Keep related projects in one window, switch from the toolbar, then split editors and terminals, drag tabs between panes, resize, and maximize.
features.04title: Use a terminal built for real workflows.
features.04desc: Full VT100/xterm emulation with tabs, themes, TUI support, clickable links, a global quick terminal, and display recovery that preserves the running shell.
features.05title: Keep changes, git, and diagnostics in view.
features.05desc: Live file reloads, sidebar status, gutter and inline diffs, blame, branch switching, config validation, and format-on-save.
features.06desc: Auto-save, session and cursor restoration, large-file handling, auto-updates, nine localizations, VoiceOver, reduced motion, and no Electron runtime.
screenshots.title: See the whole task, not disconnected tools.

screenshots.cap0: Agent Inbox keeps work from every project in one place

screenshots.cap3: A real terminal stays beside the code, with the shell and scrollback intact

screenshots.cap4: Review source and rendered output side by side

manifesto.title: Not an AI IDE. A native editor that understands when agents are working.
manifesto.desc: Pine keeps the terminal as the source of truth and turns the editor into a live surface for code, diffs, diagnostics, and attention.
story.title: A native control surface for CLI-agent work.
story.quote: "The terminal stays open. Evidence stays attached. You stay in control."
story.body: Pine is moving toward a workspace where terminal tools remain interchangeable, agent work carries durable context, and every change can be reviewed beside the code. The editor should become more capable without becoming heavier, more opaque, or dependent on one agent.
install.title: Install Pine in 10 seconds.
install.desc: Use Homebrew, grab the latest DMG, or build from source in Xcode. Pine stays a focused native Mac app with no browser runtime.
install.shellNote: Build from source with xcodebuild -project Pine.xcodeproj -scheme Pine build if you want the full native stack on your machine.
footer.text: Pine is open source and built for macOS developers who work with code and CLI agents.
